lesson_title: The Law That Made Neighbours Into Outsiders
hook_text: 15 September 1935. With one law, half a million people lost their country without leaving it.
clip_script: Imagine your family has lived in the same town for two hundred years. Your grandfather fought for the country. Your mother is the town doctor. Then, step by step, it is taken away. Germany, 1933. A boycott of Jewish shops. Jewish teachers and judges sacked. Books burned. Then, 15 September 1935, Nuremberg. Two laws. One: only people of so-called German blood can be citizens. Jewish Germans lose the vote, their rights, their country, without moving an inch. Two: Jews and other Germans may not marry. And how did they decide who was Jewish? Not by any test. There is none. They checked your grandparents' religion. A Christian with Jewish grandparents was classed as Jewish. The race idea was a lie. Three years later, Kristallnacht: synagogues burned, shops smashed, 30 000 men sent to camps. Families tried to flee. Most countries shut their doors. Persecution does not start with violence. It starts with small steps nobody stops.
visual_style: A family photo in a town square; signs appear on a shop window; a stamp marks a document no longer citizen; a family tree with grandparents highlighted; broken glass glitters on a dark street; a door closes.
pacing: Slow, deliberate build; a pause at the grandparents; a heavy close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson for the Nuremberg Laws, Kristallnacht and the other groups the Nazis persecuted.
